title: Grade 4 Math — Fri, May 22
description: Fractions — Day 5 of 5: Synthesis — all fraction concepts
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A class of 30 students: 2/5 are boys. How many boys are there?
Riya's garden: 1/4 roses, 1/3 tulips, rest sunflowers. What fraction are sunflowers?
Convert 2 and 3/4 to improper, then add 5/4.
Arjun has 3/4 kg of sugar. He uses 1/3 kg. How much is left?
Which fraction is between 1/2 and 3/4?
questions.explanation: 1/2 = 4/8, 3/4 = 6/8. 5/8 is between 4/8 and 6/8. So 5/8 is between 1/2 and 3/4.

questions.question: A tank is 5/6 full. 1/4 of it is used. How much is left?
A rope is 2 and 3/5 m. Another is 1 and 4/5 m. Total length?
If 3/5 of a number is 18, what is the number?
Which statement is TRUE?
options: All improper fractions are greater than 1
All proper fractions are greater than 1
Mixed numbers are always less than 1
questions.explanation: Improper fractions (numerator ≥ denominator) are always ≥ 1. Proper fractions are always less than 1.

questions.question: A bag had 24 marbles. 1/3 were red, 1/4 were blue, rest were green. How many green?

questions.explanation: 5/3 × 3/5 = 15/15 = 1. A fraction multiplied by its reciprocal always equals 1.

questions.question: Week synthesis: which sentence about fractions is MOST complete?
options: Fractions show parts of a whole; can be added (same denom), compared, simplified, and converted between mixed and improper forms
Fractions are only parts of circles
You can only add fractions if they are the same
Fractions are less important than whole numbers
questions.explanation: Fractions describe parts, can be compared, added/subtracted (with common denom), simplified, and converted — a rich concept!
